Do your eyes water while watching TV? 📺💧
Sounds opposite, but it's true — watery eyes often mean your eyes are TOO DRY.
When your tear film is unstable from dryness, your eyes overreact and produce reflex tears. That's watery eyes = dry eye disease.
Signs to check:
• Watering while watching TV / screen
• Burning or gritty feeling
• Blurred vision that clears after blinking
It's not normal. Get your tear film checked.

Headaches after a full day on laptop? 💻🤦‍♀️
It's often digital eye strain — your eye muscles working too hard from screen focus, less blinking, and close distance.
Try this today:
👁️ 20-20-20 Rule — Every 20 mins, look 20 feet away for 20 sec
💧 Blink Often — Screens cut blink rate by half
📏 Arm's Length — Keep screen at arm's distance, slightly below eye level
Small habits = big relief. If headaches persist, get your eyes checked.

How often should I get my eyes checked? 👁️📅
It's not one-size-fits-all — here's a simple guide:
• UNDER 40: Healthy eyes — Once a year | Glasses/contacts / 6hr+ screen — Once a year
• 40-60: Presbyopia starts — Every 12 months | Over 60 — Every 6-12 months
• HIGH RISK: Diabetes / BP / Family h/o Glaucoma — Every 6 months | Sudden blur / pain / flashes — Check immediately
Once a year if you're under 40, more often if you have diabetes or family history!
Not one-size-fits-all — mark your calendar. 🗓️

• Crusty lids in morning
